paragraphs: Astronics Corporation ("Astronics" or the "Company") is a leading provider of advanced technologies to the global aerospace, defense, and electronics industries. Our products and services include advanced, high-performance electrical power generation, distribution and motion systems, lighting and safety systems, avionics products, systems certification, aircraft structures and automated test systems.

We have principal operations in the United States ("U.S."), Canada, France and Germany, as well as engineering offices in Ukraine and India. Our operation in Ukraine is a small engineering office and we have not experienced any significant disruption in staffing or services as a result of the continuing Ukrainian and Russian conflict.

The Company has two reportable segments, Aerospace and Test Systems. The Aerospace segment designs and manufactures products for the global aerospace and defense industry. Our Test Systems segment designs, develops, manufactures and maintains automated test systems that support the aerospace and defense, communications and mass transit industries.

Our Aerospace segment designs and manufactures products for the global aerospace industry. Product lines include lighting and safety systems, electrical power generation, distribution and seat motion systems, aircraft structures, avionics products, systems certification, and other products. Our Aerospace customers are the airframe manufacturers ("OEM") that build aircraft for the commercial transport, military and general aviation markets, suppliers to those OEMs, aircraft operators such as airlines, suppliers to the aircraft operators, and branches of the U.S. Department of Defense. During 2025, this segment's sales were divided 75% to the commercial transport market, 15% to the military aircraft market, 9% to the general aviation market and 1% to other markets. Most of this segment's sales are a result of contracts or purchase orders received from customers, placed on a day-to-day basis or for a single year procurement rather than long-term multi-year contract commitments. On occasion, the Company does receive contractual commitments or blanket purchase orders from our customers covering multiple-year deliveries of hardware to our customers.

Our Test Systems segment designs, develops, manufactures and maintains automated test systems that support the aerospace and defense, communications and mass transit industries as well as training and simulation devices for both commercial and military applications. In the Test Systems segment, Astronics' products are sold to a global customer base including OEMs and prime government contractors for both electronics and military products. The nature of our Test Systems business is such that it pursues large, often multi-year, projects.

Sales by segment, geographic region, major customer and foreign operations are provided in Note 20, Segments, to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8, Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, of this report.

We have a significant concentration of business with one major customer, The Boeing Company ("Boeing"). Sales to Boeing accounted for 10.4% of sales in 2025, 10.2% of sales in 2024, and 11.0% of sales in 2023. Sales to Boeing are primarily in the Aerospace segment.

Our strategy is to increase our value by developing technologies and capabilities either internally or through acquisition, and use those capabilities to provide innovative solutions to our targeted markets where our technology can be beneficial.

On June 30, 2025, the Company purchased the membership interests of Envoy Aerospace, LLC ("Envoy Aerospace"), located in Aurora, Illinois. Envoy Aerospace is an FAA Organization Designation Authorization ("ODA") services provider. Envoy Aerospace is included in our Aerospace segment. The total purchase price was approximately $8.3 million, net of cash acquired and the estimated closing adjustment. Of the purchase price, $4.5 million was paid at the closing date. Payments of $2.0 million and $1.8 million will become payable by the Company following the first and second anniversary of the closing date, respectively, based on the achievement of certain milestones.

On October 13, 2025, the Company acquired all of the issued and outstanding capital stock of Bühler Motor Aviation ("BMA"), located in Uhldingen-Mühlhofen, Germany. BMA is an established manufacturer of aircraft seat actuation systems with a broad product portfolio that includes actuators, electronics, control panels, pneumatic systems, and lighting. BMA is included in our Aerospace segment. The total purchase price was approximately $18.0 million, net of cash acquired and the estimated closing adjustment. The purchase price was paid at the closing date.

On February 13, 2019, the Company completed a divestiture of its semiconductor test business within the Test Systems segment. The total proceeds of the divestiture included contingent purchase consideration ("earnout"). In March 2023, the Company agreed with a final earnout calculation in the amount of $3.4 million. The Company recorded the gain and received the payment in the first quarter of 2023. We are not eligible for any further earnout payments related to this divestiture.
Liquidity is discussed under the heading "Liquidity and Capital Resources", in Item 7, Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations, of this report.
The following is a summary of the terms of our principal existing indebtedness as of December 31, 2025:

•Revolving Credit Facility: On October 22, 2025, Company entered into a $300.0 million senior secured cash flow-based revolving credit facility (the "Revolving Credit Facility") that replaced its previous $220.0 million asset-based revolving credit facility (the "ABL Revolving Credit Facility"), which had been subject to a borrowing base tied to eligible assets. The Company pays interest on the unpaid principal amount outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility at a rate equal to Term SOFR plus an applicable margin ranging from 1.25% to 2.125% determined based upon the Company's Total Net Debt Leverage Ratio (as defined in the Revolving Credit Facility agreement).

Our business faces many risks, and you should carefully consider the following risk factors, together with all of the other information included in this report, including the financial statements and related notes contained in Item 8, Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, and discussion in Item 7, Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations, when deciding to invest in us. Any of the risks discussed below, or elsewhere in this report or in our other SEC filings, could have a material impact on our business, financial condition or results of operations. Additional risks not currently known to us or that we currently consider immaterial also may materially adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations in the future. As a result, the trading price of our common stock could decline, and you could lose all or part of your investment in our common stock.

The loss of Boeing as a major customer or a significant reduction in business with this customer would reduce our sales and earnings. In 2025, 2024, and 2023 we had a concentration of sales to Boeing representing approximately 10.4%, 10.2%, and 11.0% of our sales, respectively. Revenue earned from sales to Boeing may decline or fluctuate significantly in the future. We may not be able to offset any decline in sales from Boeing with sales from new customers or other existing customers. The loss of Boeing as a customer or a significant reduction in business with Boeing would significantly reduce our sales and earnings. Accordingly, a portion of our potential for success will depend on our continued ability to develop and manage our relationship with Boeing.

The markets we serve are cyclical and sensitive to domestic and foreign economic conditions, conflicts and events, which may cause our operating results to fluctuate. The markets we serve are sensitive to fluctuations in general business cycles, global pandemics, domestic and foreign governmental tariffs, trade and monetary policies, national and international conflicts, and economic conditions and events. Any new pandemic or other future public health crisis, and efforts to contain such public health crises, could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.

In our Aerospace segment, demand by the general aviation markets for our products is dependent upon several factors, including capital investment, product innovations, economic growth and wealth creation and technology upgrades. The commercial aerospace market is a global duopoly where Boeing and Airbus SE ("Airbus") serve as the OEMs. Their production health is vital to our performance. Historical disruptions, such as quality control challenges and factory labor actions, have previously hindered our scalability. Future shifts in their production rates remain a primary factor in our projected results. In addition, the commercial airline industry is highly cyclical, with significant downturns in the past and sensitivity to such things as fuel price increases, labor disputes, global economic conditions, availability of capital to fund new aircraft purchase and

upgrades of existing aircraft and passenger demand. Any change in these factors could result in a further reduction in the amount of discretionary air travel and the ability of airlines to invest in new aircraft or to upgrade existing aircraft. Therefore, our business is directly affected by economic factors outside of our control and other trends that affect our customers in the commercial aerospace industry. These factors could reduce orders for new aircraft and could reduce airline investment in cabin upgrades for which we supply products, thus reducing our sales and profits. A reduction in air travel may also result in our commercial airline customers being unable to pay our invoices on a timely basis or at all.

We are a supplier on various new aircraft programs just entering or expected to begin production in the future. As with any new program, there is risk as to whether the aircraft or program will be successful and accepted by the market. As is customary for our industry, we purchase inventory and invest in specific capital equipment to support our production requirements generally based on delivery schedules provided by our customer. If a program or aircraft is not successful, we may have to write-off all or a part of the inventory, accounts receivable and capital equipment related to the program. A write-off of these assets could result in a significant reduction of earnings and cause covenant violations relating to our debt agreements. This could result in our being unable to borrow additional funds under our Revolving Credit Facility or being obliged to refinance or renegotiate our indebtedness on potentially unfavorable terms for us.

paragraphs: Astronics Corporation, through its subsidiaries, is a leading supplier of advanced technologies and products to the global aerospace and defense industries. Our products and services include advanced, high-performance electrical power generation and distribution systems, seat motion solutions, lighting and safety systems, avionics products, aircraft structures, systems certification, and automated test systems.

We have two reportable segments, Aerospace and Test Systems. Our Aerospace segment has principal operating facilities in the United States, Canada, France and Germany and an engineering office in Ukraine. Our Test Systems segment has principal operating facilities in the United States and an engineering office in India.

Our Aerospace segment designs and manufactures products for the global aerospace industry. Product lines include lighting and safety systems, electrical power generation, distribution and seat motion systems, aircraft structures, avionics products, systems certification, and other products. Our primary Aerospace customers are the airframe manufacturers ("OEM") that build aircraft for the commercial transport, military and general aviation markets, suppliers to those OEMs, aircraft operators such as airlines, suppliers to the aircraft operators, and branches of the U.S. Department of Defense ("USDOD"). Our Test Systems segment designs, develops, manufactures and maintains automated test systems that support the aerospace and defense and mass transit industries. In the Test Systems segment, Astronics' products are sold to a global customer base including OEMs and prime government contractors for both electronics and military products.

Our strategy is to increase our value by developing technologies and capabilities, either internally or through acquisition, and using those capabilities to provide innovative solutions to our targeted markets where our technology can be beneficial.

Important factors affecting our growth and profitability are the rate at which new aircraft are produced, government funding and timing of awards of military programs, our ability to have our products designed into new aircraft, the rates at which aircraft owners, including commercial airlines, refurbish or install upgrades to their aircraft and supply chain and labor market pressures. New aircraft build rates and aircraft owners' spending on upgrades and refurbishments is cyclical and dependent on the strength of the global economy. Once one of our products is designed into a new aircraft, the spare parts business associated thereto is also frequently retained by the Company. Future growth and profitability of the Test Systems business is dependent on developing and procuring new and follow-on business. The nature of our Test Systems business is such that it pursues large, often multi-year, projects. There can be significant periods of time between orders in this business, which may result in large fluctuations of sales and profit levels and backlog from period to period. Test Systems segment customers include the USDOD, prime contractors to the USDOD, mass transit operators and prime contractors to mass transit operators.

Each of the markets that we serve presents opportunities that we expect will provide growth for the Company over the long-term. We continue to look for opportunities in all of our markets to capitalize on our core competencies to expand our existing business and to grow through strategic acquisitions.

The main challenges that we continue to face include varying levels of supply chain pressures, material availability and cost increases (including costs associated with the imposition of tariffs by the United States and other countries discussed herein), labor availability and cost, and improving shareholder value through increasing profitability. Increasing profitability is dependent on many things, primarily sales growth, both acquired and organic, and the Company's ability to pass cost increases along to customers and control operating expenses, and to identify means of creating improved productivity. Sales are driven by increased build rates for existing aircraft, market acceptance and economic success of new aircraft and our products, continued government funding of defense programs, the Company's ability to obtain production contracts for parts we currently supply or
have been selected to design and develop for new aircraft platforms and continually identifying and winning new business for our Test Systems segment.

Reduced aircraft build rates driven by regulatory actions impacting OEM production, a weak economy, aircraft groundings, tight credit markets, reduced air passenger travel, tariffs impacting OEM demand, and an increasing supply of used aircraft on the market would likely result in reduced demand for our products, which will result in lower profits. Reduction of defense spending may result in fewer opportunities for us to compete, which could result in lower profits in the future. Many of our newer development programs are based on new and unproven technology and at the same time we are challenged to develop the technology on a schedule that is consistent with specific programs. Delays in delivery schedules and incremental costs resulting from tariffs and other trade policy matters, supply chain pressures, and labor market pressures have in the past resulted in, and could in the future also result in, lower profits. We will continue to address these challenges by working to improve operating efficiencies and focusing on executing on the growth opportunities currently in front of us.

On October 22, 2025, the Company entered into the $300 million senior secured Revolving Credit Facility. The Revolving Credit Facility replaced the Company's ABL Revolving Credit Facility which was terminated on October 22, 2025. The Revolving Credit Facility subjects us to various financial and other affirmative and negative covenants with which we must comply on an ongoing or periodic basis. These include financial covenants pertaining to a total leverage ratio, a consolidated interest coverage ratio, and a secured net debt leverage ratio requirement. An unexpected decline in our revenues or operating income, including occurring as a result of events beyond our control, could cause us to violate our financial covenants.

See Item 1A, Risk Factors, of this report for an additional discussion of risks associated with our potential inability to satisfy the financial and restrictive covenants set forth in the Revolving Credit Facility.

Challenges affecting the commercial aviation industry or key participants can adversely impact the demand for our products and services, the timing of orders, deliveries and related payments and other factors. We are monitoring the production levels and anticipated ramp-ups at Boeing and Airbus, and we continue to align our operations with their production expectations.

We are monitoring the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine, as well as other geopolitical tensions and conflicts around the world, and the potential impact of related export controls, financial and economic sanctions, and other restrictions imposed by the U.S., the U.K., the European Union, and other countries. While the Russia-Ukraine conflict has not resulted in a direct material adverse impact on our business to date, the implications of both this and other global conflicts in the short-term and long-term are difficult to predict. Factors such as increased energy costs, disruptions in the availability of certain raw materials, restrictions on air travel or trade with affected regions, sanctions on companies or industries, shifts in customer stability, and broader impacts on the global economy and aviation sector could pose risks to our operations and financial performance.

In October 2024, a customer reported within the Aerospace segment declared bankruptcy. As a result, the Company recorded a full reserve of $1.0 million for outstanding receivables, a reserve of $1.7 million for inventory and $0.6 million for impairment of fixed assets. In November 2023, a non-core contract manufacturing customer reported within the Aerospace segment filed for bankruptcy under Chapter 11. As a result, the Company recorded a full reserve of $7.5 million for outstanding accounts receivable and a reserve of $3.6 million for inventory.

paragraphs: Astronics Corporation ("Astronics" or the "Company") 為全球航空、防禦及電子產業提供先進技術的領導廠商。我們的產品與服務包括先進、高性能的電氣發電、分配及運動系統、照明與安全系統、航電產品、系統認證、飛機結構與自動測試系統。
我們的主要營運據點位於美國 ("U.S."), 加拿大、法國與德國，並在烏克蘭與印度設有工程辦事處。我們在烏克蘭的營運為小型工程辦事處，且因烏克蘭與俄羅斯衝突持續進行，我們尚未遭遇任何重大的人力或服務中斷情況。
本公司有兩個應報告分部，為航空與測試系統。航空分部設計與製造產品用於全球航空與防禦產業。我們的測試系統分部設計、開發、製造與維護自動測試系統，以支援航空與防禦、通訊與大眾運輸產業。

我們的航空分部設計與製造產品用於全球航空產業。產品線包括照明與安全系統、電氣發電、分配與座椅運動系統、飛機結構、航電產品、系統認證及其他產品。我們的航空客戶為飛機製造商 ("OEM")，這些製造商為商業客運、軍事與一般航空市場製造飛機，以及這些 OEM 的供應商、飛機營運者如航空公司、飛機營運者的供應商，以及美國國防部的分支機構。在 2025 年，此分部的銷售額中，75% 來自商業客運市場，15% 來自軍用飛機市場，9% 來自一般航空市場，1% 來自其他市場。此分部的銷售額大多來自客戶每日或單年採購的契約或訂單，而非長期多年度契約承諾。有時，本公司會收到客戶的契約承諾或總括採購訂單，涵蓋多年度的硬體交付。
我們的測試系統分部設計、開發、製造與維護自動測試系統，以支援航空與防禦、通訊與大眾運輸產業，以及用於商業與軍事應用的訓練與模擬裝置。在測試系統分部，Astronics 的產品銷售給全球客戶羣，包括 OEM 與主要政府承包商，用於電子與軍事產品。我們測試系統業務的性質，使其追求大型、往往為多年度的專案。
段落銷售、地理區域、主要客戶與海外營運資料，請參閱第 20 註，段落，於第 8 項，財務資料與補充資料，本報告的財務報表中。
我們與一主要客戶有顯著的業務集中度，為 The Boeing Company ("Boeing")。2025 年銷售額中，銷售給 Boeing 佔 10.4%，2024 年為 10.2%，2023 年為 11.0%。銷售給 Boeing 的業務主要來自航空分部。
我們的策略為透過內部開發或收購技術與能力，以增加我們的價值，並運用這些能力為我們目標市場提供創新解決方案，使我們的技術能發揮效益。

於 2025 年 6 月 30 日，本公司購入位於伊利諾州奧羅拉（Aurora, Illinois）之 Envoy Aerospace, LLC（"Envoy Aerospace"）之股東權益。Envoy Aerospace 為美國聯邦航空管理局（FAA）組織設計授權（"ODA"）服務供應商。Envoy Aerospace 納入本公司之航空應報告分部。總購併價格約為 8.3 百萬美元，扣除所取得現金及預估關閉調整後之金額。購併價格中，4.5 百萬美元於關閉日支付。本公司將於關閉日後第一及第二個週年日分別支付 2.0 百萬美元及 1.8 百萬美元，依特定里程碑之達成情況為準。

於 2025 年 10 月 13 日，本公司取得位於德國烏爾丁根-穆爾霍芬（Uhldingen-Mühlhofen）之 Bühler Motor Aviation（"BMA"）所有已發行及流通之資本股票。BMA 為已建立之飛機座椅作動系統製造商，其產品組合廣泛，包括作動器、電子元件、控制面板、氣壓系統及照明設備。BMA 納入本公司之航空應報告分部。總購併價格約為 18.0 百萬美元，扣除所取得現金及預估關閉調整後之金額。購併價格於關閉日支付。
於 2019 年 2 月 13 日，本公司完成其測試系統分部內之半導體測試業務之出售。該出售之總所得包含附條件購併對價（"earnout"）。於 2023 年 3 月，本公司與最終 earnout 計算金額 3.4 百萬美元達成協議。本公司於 2023 年第一季確認獲利並收到該筆付款。本公司就此出售業務不再有進一步 earnout 付款之資格。
流動性於本報告之 "流動性及資本資源" 章節（第 7 項，管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析）中討論。
以下為本公司截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日主要現有債務之條款摘要：

•週轉信貸融資：於 2025 年 10 月 22 日，本公司與銀行簽訂 300.0 百萬美元之高階 secured 現金流量基週轉信貸融資（"週轉信貸融資"），取代其先前 220.0 百萬美元之資產基週轉信貸融資（"ABL 週轉信貸融資"），該筆融資係以可資抵押之資產為基礎。本公司就週轉信貸融資未償還之本金金額支付利息，利率為 Term SOFR 加上適用之幅度，幅度範圍為 1.25% 至 2.125%，依本公司之總淨負債槓桿比率（如週轉信貸融資協議中所定義）而定。

paragraphs: Astronics Corporation, 透過其子公司，為全球航空與防禦產業提供先進技術與產品的領導供應商。我們的產品與服務包括先進、高性能的電氣發電與配電系統、座椅運動解決方案、照明與安全系統、航電產品、飛機結構、系統認證及自動化測試系統。
我們有兩個應報告分部，為航空與測試系統。我們的航空分部主要營運設施位於美國、加拿大、法國與德國，並在烏克蘭設有工程辦事處。我們的測試系統分部主要營運設施位於美國，並在印度設有工程辦事處。

我們的航空分部設計與製造產品用於全球航空產業。產品線包括照明與安全系統、電氣發電、配電與座椅運動系統、飛機結構、航電產品、系統認證及其他產品。我們的主要航空客戶為飛機製造商（"OEM"），這些製造商為商業運輸、軍事與一般航空市場製造飛機，以及這些OEM的供應商、飛機營運者如航空公司、飛機營運者的供應商，以及美國國防部（"USDOD"）的分支機構。我們的測試系統分部設計、開發、製造與維護自動化測試系統，以支援航空與防禦及大眾運輸產業。在測試系統分部，Astronics的產品銷售給全球客戶羣，包括OEM與主要政府承包商，用於電子與軍事產品。
我們的策略為透過內部開發或收購技術與能力，來提升我們的價值，並運用這些能力為我們目標市場提供創新解決方案，使我們的技術能發揮效益。

影響本公司成長與獲利的重要因素包括新飛機的生產速度、政府資金及軍事計畫的獎勵時間、本公司產品被設計進新飛機的能力、飛機所有者（包括商業航空公司） refurbish 或安裝升級裝置的速率，以及供應鏈與勞動市場壓力。新飛機的建造速度與飛機所有者在升級與 refurbish 上的支出具有週期性，並取決於總體經濟的強弱。一旦本公司產品被設計進新飛機，與之相關的備件業務通常也會由本公司保留。測試系統業務的未來成長與獲利取決於開發與取得新業務及續約業務。測試系統業務的性質為追求大型、往往為多年度的專案。此業務可能在訂單之間有相當長的時間間隔，這可能會導致銷售與獲利水準出現大幅波動，以及各期間的積壓訂單。測試系統業務的客戶包括美國國防部（USDOD）、USDOD 的主要承包商、大眾捷運運營商及大眾捷運運營商的主要承包商。
我們服務的每個市場都提供了我們預期將在長遠提供成長機會的潛力。我們持續尋找所有市場的機會，以利用我們的核心競爭優勢來擴展現有業務，並透過戰略收購來成長。

我們持續面臨的主要挑戰包括供應鏈壓力的不一致程度、材料可得性與成本增加（包括與美國及其他國家 herein 所討論的關稅措施相關的成本）、勞動力可得性與成本，以及透過提高獲利來改善股東價值。提高獲利取決於許多因素，主要為銷售成長（包括取得與內生性成長），以及本公司將成本增加轉嫁給客戶的能力與控制營運費用，以及尋找提高生產力的方法。銷售受到現有飛機建造速度增加、新飛機市場接受度與經濟成功，以及本公司產品，以及政府對防禦計畫的持續資金支持的推動，以及本公司取得我們目前供應或已被選定設計與開發的新飛機平台的生產合同的能力，以及持續識別與取得測試系統業務的新業務的影響。
have been selected to design and develop for new aircraft platforms and continually identifying and winning new business for our Test Systems segment.

因監管行動影響原廠生產、總體經濟疲軟、飛機停飛、信貸市場緊縮、航空乘客旅遊減少、影響原廠需求的關稅，以及市場上使用飛機供應增加，導致飛機建造速度下降，可能導致我們產品需求減少，進而導致利潤降低。防禦性支出減少可能導致我們競爭機會減少，進而導致未來利潤降低。我們許多較新的開發計畫都基於新且未經驗證的技術，同時我們也面臨在符合特定計畫的時間表下開發技術的挑戰。因關稅和其他貿易政策事項、供應鏈壓力和勞動市場壓力導致的交付時間延遲和額外成本，在過去已導致利潤降低，未來也可能導致利潤降低。我們將持續透過改善營運效率和專注於執行目前面臨的成長機會來應對這些挑戰。

2025年10月22日，本公司與電信業者簽訂了300百萬美元的高階抵押循環信貸融資協議。該循環信貸融資協議取代了本公司於2025年10月22日終止的ABL循環信貸融資協議。該循環信貸融資協議使我們必須遵守各種財務及其他積極與負面契約條款，並持續或定期遵守。這些包括財務契約條款，涉及總負債比率、合併利息覆蓋比率及抵押淨負債比率要求。若我們的營收或營運收入意外下降，包括因超出我們控制範圍的事件所致，可能會導致我們違反財務契約條款。
請參閱本報告第1A項「風險因素」，以瞭解與我們潛在無法符合循環信貸融資協議中規定的財務及限制性契約條款相關的風險進一步討論。
影響商業航空產業或關鍵參與者的挑戰，可能對我們產品及服務的需求、訂單時間、交付及相關付款，以及其他因素產生負面影響。我們正在監測波音與空中巴士的生產量及預期增加情況，並持續調整我們的營運以符合其生產預期。

我們正在監測俄羅斯與烏克蘭之間的持續衝突，以及全球其他地緣政治緊張與衝突，以及相關出口管制、財務與經濟制裁及其他限制措施的潛在影響，這些措施由美國、英國、歐盟及其他國家所實施。儘管俄羅斯與烏克蘭衝突迄今尚未對我們業務造成直接且重大的負面影響，但此衝突及其他全球衝突在短期與長期的影響，難以預測。例如能源成本上升、某些原材料供應中斷、對受影響地區的航空旅行或貿易限制、對公司或產業的制裁、客戶穩定性變化，以及對全球經濟與航空產業的廣泛影響，都可能對我們的營運與財務表現造成風險。
2024年10月，航空業務部門的一位客戶聲稱破產。因此，本公司針對未收帳款記錄了1.0百萬美元的完全備抵，針對存貨記錄了1.7百萬美元的備抵，以及針對固定資產減損記錄了0.6百萬美元。2023年11月，航空業務部門的一家非核心合同製造客戶根據第11章聲請破產保護。因此，本公司針對未收帳款記錄了7.5百萬美元的完全備抵，並針對存貨記錄了3.6百萬美元的備抵。

paragraphs: 本公司業務面臨許多風險，您應仔細考慮下列風險因素，並與本報告中包含的所有其他資訊一併考量，包括第 8 項「財務報表及補充資料」所載的財務報表及相關附註，以及第 7 項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」所載的討論。下列任一風險或本報告或本公司其他 SEC 檔案中所討論的其他風險，都可能對本公司業務、財務狀況或營運成果產生重大影響。此外，尚有其他風險，目前本公司尚未知悉或目前認為不重要，這些風險在未來也可能對本公司業務、財務狀況或營運成果產生重大不利影響。因此，本公司普通股的交易價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資於本公司普通股的金額。

失去波音為主要客戶，或與此客戶的業務大幅減少，將導致本公司銷售額與獲利減少。2025 年、2024 年及 2023 年，本公司對波音的銷售集中度分別約為銷售額的 10.4%、10.2% 及 11.0%。未來來自波音的銷售收入可能減少或大幅波動。本公司可能無法以新客戶或其他現有客戶的銷售來彌補來自波音銷售的減少。失去波音為客戶或與波音的業務大幅減少，將會顯著降低本公司銷售額與獲利。因此，本公司未來成功潛力的一部分將取決於本公司持續發展與管理與波音關係的能力。
我們所服務的市場為週期性市場，且對國內外經濟狀況、衝突與事件相當敏感，這可能導致我們的營運成果波動。我們所服務的市場對一般商業週期的波動、全球疫情、國內外政府關稅、貿易與貨幣政策、國家與國際衝突，以及經濟狀況與事件相當敏感。任何新的疫情或其他未來公共衛生危機，以及對這些公共衛生危機的應對措施，都可能對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運成果產生重大不利影響。

在本公司航空器應報告分部，一般航空市場對我們產品的需求取決於多種因素，包括資本投資、產品創新、經濟成長與財富創造以及技術升級。商業航空器市場為全球雙頭市場，波音與空中巴士股份有限公司（"空中巴士"）為 OEM。他們的生產狀況對我們的表現至關重要。過去的幹擾，例如品質控制問題與工廠勞動罷工，曾導致我們的擴張能力受阻。未來他們的生產速率變動仍是我們預測結果的主要因素。此外，商業航空業為高度週期性產業，過去曾有顯著的衰退，且對燃油價格上漲、勞資爭議、全球經濟狀況、資金可得性以支應新機購置以及現有機隊升級與乘客需求等事項相當敏感。
任何這些因素的變動都可能導致進一步減少自由支配的航空旅行，以及航空公司投資新機或升級現有機隊的能力。因此，我們的業務直接受到我們無法控制的經濟因素及其他影響商業航空業客戶的趨勢影響。這些因素可能減少新機訂單，也可能減少航空公司對我們供應產品的客艙升級投資，從而減少我們的銷售與獲利。航空旅行減少也可能導致我們的商業航空客戶無法按時或完全支付我們的應收款項。

我們是許多即將進入或預期將開始生產的新飛機計畫的供應商。如同任何新計畫一樣，這些飛機或計畫是否成功並被市場接受存在風險。根據我們產業的慣例，我們通常根據客戶提供的交貨排程，購買存貨並投資特定的資本設備，以支持我們的生產需求。如果某個計畫或飛機未能成功，我們可能必須核銷與該計畫相關的全部或部分存貨、應收款項及資本設備。這些資產的核銷可能導致獲利大幅減少，並導致違反我們債務協議中的契約條款。這可能導致我們無法在循環信貸融資協議下進一步取得資金，或被迫重新融資或重新協商我們的債務，而這對我們而言可能在條款上不利。
